items.title: Danny Barker Interview, 1976-02-04
items.q: Standard, Chick Webb, Savoy, Borrow for six, seven, eight years, you dig?

ctx.x: Do you, do you think that, that Jelly Roll Morton had the wide popularity among blacks that Louis Armstrong did when he was alive?

Never, never, never, never. Jelly, Jelly played in, clubs, and he made records that were popular, but to actually have, he moved around too fast. See, if he just stayed like, in Chicago, and worked in clubs, they stationary, like you make a reputation in the town, like Fletcher Henderson was in New York, Cab Calloway were in New York at the Cotton Club, Fletcher at the Roseland, you heard him on the radio, Duke was at the Cotton Club, you heard him on the radio, Earl Hines in, in the Grand Terrace in Chicago for…

do you think that, do you think that, that Louis Armstrong, was able to, keep his reputation, even though he traveled, or do you think that he built, his reputation in Chicago, and then when he traveled, it was already behind him?

items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Chick Webb's got a guitar player... John Trueheart with Chick Webb. He was the master. Everybody went to hear him. They see him just chomp on that guitar with Chick Webb.

ctx.x: In Harlem. It’s a club on 133rd Street. Later it became Dickie Wells’s nightclub. It was on a basement on the ground floor with a club called the . . . a funny name. The Fun Box? No. The Fun Box is near . . . The Mad House, on the first floor. The Mad

House. Downstairs was the Nest Club. I played in there. You go to work at ten o’clock at night and you come out ten o’clock in the morning, because it was a depression that set in, and we didn’t get a crowd until after three o’clock in the morning. Three, four, five . . . five o’clock, the band go on, because you sit there all night. There might be parties drifting in. It was just to winter. I had never seen snow, real snow falling. The doorman there, he had seven singers there: Mamie Smith, Clara Smith, and…

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: Chick Webb hired him [Big Green] for a while

ctx.x: No. That was where I saw Jabbo. All these people was in a gin mill on Seventh Avenue down in a basement, and I'm in there. And Big Green is in there, and he's drunk, and he'd lost his weight, and he said ain't nobody would hire him after Fletcher, and Chick Webb hired him for a while but he couldn't depend on him...
Big Green the trombone player, yeah..
